forbidden_inferences: No temperature, pH, dissolved-oxygen, or hydraulic response.
No claim that a single microbial guild exclusively performs the process.
No direct use of the existing one-step ammonium-to-nitrate assertion.

proposed_assertion.claim_text: During aerobic nitrification, ammonia/ammonium nitrogen can be oxidized to nitrite nitrogen as the first oxidation step.

review_requirements: Verify exact source metadata and source lineage.
Review the proposed claim wording against both primary sources.
Verify subject/object scientific entity identities and elemental-N basis.
Review TAN-N to ammonia/ammonium semantic bridge separately.
Only after the semantic bridge is accepted may process alignment be reviewed.
Record reviewer identity, decision, timestamp, and review artifact SHA.

semantic_bridge.issue: The mechanism papers support ammonia/ammonium oxidation to nitrite, whereas the RATE-1F source component is the analytical TAN-N pool. A reviewed semantic bridge is required before process-specific scientific support can be marked reviewed.

authors: Maartje A. H. J. van Kessel
Huub J. M. Op den Camp
sources.evidence_summary: The paper describes nitrification as a two-step process in which ammonia is first oxidized to nitrite and then nitrite is oxidized to nitrate; it also experimentally demonstrates complete ammonium oxidation via nitrite in Nitrospira.
sources.title: Complete nitrification by a single microorganism

sources.evidence_summary: The paper describes nitrification as oxidation of ammonia via nitrite to nitrate and experimentally characterizes a Nitrospira organism encoding and expressing both ammonia- and nitrite-oxidation pathways.
sources.title: Complete nitrification by Nitrospira bacteria
